chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, the followers of Ja'far are those whose stomach is chaste (from unlawful food), whose private part is chaste (from adultery), whose striving is intense, who work for their Creator, who hope for His reward, and who fear His punishment. So when you see those people, those are the followers of Ja'far. And I have written what I narrated on this meaning in the book Sifat al-Shi'a.

key_terms.شِيعَةُ جَعْفَرٍ: Followers of Ja'far (specifically Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.صِفَاتِ الشِّيعَةِ: The Characteristics of the Followers (title of a book by the compiler)

ai.seo_question: What are the five characteristics of true followers of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq according to hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that true Shi'a identity is defined by ethical and spiritual rigor rather than mere nominal affiliation, emphasizing self-restraint (chastity), active devotion (jihad), and a balanced state of hope and fear (tawakkul). This narration serves as a foundational criterion in Shia theology for distinguishing genuine adherents through their practical application of faith in daily conduct and afterlife orientation.
